newsitem.title: USA: US legislator to file bank reform bill Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: US legislator to file bank reform bill Tuesday.

text.p: House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach will introduce a legislative proposal Tuesday to overhaul U.S. financial regulations, a spokesman for the committee said.
The Iowa Republican has long supported breaching the wall between banks and other financial institutions enacted by the Glass-Steagall Act of 1933.
In a speech last month, Leach said his bill would allow banks to affiliate with securities firms and insurance companies under a holding company structure regulated by the Federal Reserve.
But commercial firms outside of the finance industry would not be allowed to affiliate with or own banks, Leach said.
The bill would also include a merger of thrift and bank charters, Leach said last month.
After Congress failed to enact similiar legislation last year, regulators have moved to provide some greater leeway to banks.
The Federal Reserve voted Dec 20 to allow certain bank subsidiaries to derive as much as 25 percent of their revenue from underwriting activity, up from a previous limit of 10 percent.
And Office of the Comptroller of the Currency announced Nov 20 a policy to allow nationally-chartered bank affiliates to engage in a wide variety of non-banking activities.
